# Migrate a project generated by an older template

> **Draft — not yet a tested migration guide.** The proposed target is MCP 2026-07-28 with C# SDK 2.4.0 on .NET 10. The template code has not been upgraded at this documentation checkpoint, and the steps below have not yet been tested on a generated application. Do not use this draft for a production rollout.

## Do I need to migrate?

**No. Migration is your choice.** Releasing or installing a newer template does not modify projects you already generated. This guide is for owners who want to update their existing application manually.

This does not promise maintenance or security coverage for older versions. Review security updates separately from deciding whether to adopt the new protocol.

The starting point covered here is an application generated from `EasyMcp.McpServer.Template` 1.4.0, using C# SDK 1.3.0 and .NET 10. If your versions differ, check them first. Technical references and customized-server cases are in the [advanced notes](mcp-2026-07-28-advanced.md).

## 1. Save a working version

Create a branch before changing anything:

```bash
git switch -c upgrade-mcp
```

Commit your current application changes, without credentials, and keep the last working deployment if you have one. Then run your existing checks:

```bash
dotnet restore
dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore
dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build
```

Resolve or record existing failures before continuing so you can tell them apart from migration problems.

## 2. Update the shared package versions

Open your application's `Directory.Build.props`. Update these existing properties:

```xml
<ModelContextProtocolVersion>2.4.0</ModelContextProtocolVersion>
<MicrosoftExtensionsVersion>10.0.14</MicrosoftExtensionsVersion>
<MicrosoftExtensionsHostingVersion>10.0.14</MicrosoftExtensionsHostingVersion>
<MicrosoftExtensionsConfigVersion>10.0.14</MicrosoftExtensionsConfigVersion>
```

Keep .NET 10. If you added MCP package references with their own version numbers, align those references too. The [dependency notes](mcp-2026-07-28-advanced.md#2-align-packages-not-just-one-version-string) explain customized package graphs and restore errors.

## 3. Update HTTP configuration, if you use HTTP

In your HTTP host's `Program.cs`, find the existing `.WithHttpTransport()` call and replace that call with:

```csharp
.WithHttpTransport(options =>
{
    options.SessionMode = HttpServerSessionMode.Stateless;
});
```

Add `using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore;` if it is not already present. Keep the rest of your server and tool registration unchanged; do not add a second registration.

Stateless means requests do not rely on a persistent MCP HTTP session. If you deliberately need to retain clients that depend on the old session behavior, use the [optional compatibility guidance](mcp-2026-07-28-advanced.md#3-select-an-explicit-http-compatibility-policy) instead. That is a specific compatibility choice, not a requirement for every application.

**Stdio-only application?** Skip this HTTP step. Keep its transport registration and validate it in the next step.

## 4. Build and check your application

Run the same restore, build and test commands from step 1. Review new errors or warnings rather than hiding them.

Start your application using your usual command, connect a client supporting the target protocol, and check that you can list and call your tools. Check prompts and resources if you use them. Test each transport you ship and your authentication configuration.

A successful build alone does not prove that your client and server communicate correctly. If you need older clients to keep working, test those specific clients as well; supporting every older client is not an automatic requirement of this guide.

If you added custom protocol features, authentication or response parsing, review only the relevant [advanced breaking-change notes](mcp-2026-07-28-advanced.md#5-audit-conditional-sdk-breaks-in-custom-applications).

## 5. Keep your application code

Do not regenerate the template over your project. Keep your tools, business services, namespaces, configuration and secrets.

You do not need to install the new template to update an existing application's package references and host code. If you want to compare with a fresh project after a new template is released, generate it in a separate directory and copy only the changes you actually need.

## 6. Deploy only after your checks pass

Use your normal deployment process and keep the previous working application and configuration available. If the migration fails, return to that complete working version rather than changing just one package number.

## What this guide does not do

- Update your project automatically or require you to migrate.
- Require a hybrid compatibility layer for every existing project.
- Replace your application with a newly generated scaffold.
- Add demonstrations of new protocol features; those are separate future work.

See the [advanced notes](mcp-2026-07-28-advanced.md) for session choices, custom features, detailed validation, rollback caveats and official sources.
